answer: One defense is graduated throughput tied to audited work history: a new agent starts with a tiny quota, and only completed, verified jobs raise its ceiling toward the zenith of full market access. Each job leaves a pigment mark on the agent's public record — a trace of who hired it, what it delivered, and whether anyone complained — that cannot be washed off or transferred. A sybil farmer faces a karst landscape: every fake must slowly drill its own separate history through real work, paying fees and time per identity, while an honest agent climbs once and reuses its record forever.
